Quick summary of what I pulled:
- Accounts found: 6 active accounts with @concilio.io across our system.
- Trial extension history: 4 of those accounts had a previous 30-day extension in the last 9 months.
- Billing identifiers: 2 accounts submitted different billing emails but reference the same company tax id on onboarding form (Concilio-TID-4021) — possible consolidation to bypass per-account limits.
- IP analysis: 3 distinct signups from the same /24 subnet over the past 6 weeks; 2 signups came from a cloud provider IP range (GCP) and 1 from an ISP in SF.

Preliminary verdict: patterns consistent with coordinated multi-account evaluation, potentially gaming the extension policy to increase aggregate free usage. Not conclusive but enough to pause auto-approval.

I recommend requesting additional proof-of-need (owner confirmations) and offering a scoped paid pilot instead of blanket free credits. If they push, we should escalate for a temporary hold.

Ben Carter
Senior Ops Investigator
Redwood Inference

Adding the fraud team's analysis:
- Device fingerprints indicate reuse across 4 accounts (shared browser plugins and identical viewport strings).
- Payment verification: two accounts show the same virtual card issuer (VC-07) masked; vendor reconciliation suggests these cards were created by the same payments team at Concilio.
- Past redlines: one contact (j.santos@concilio.io) appears in our escalation log from March for unusual extension requests.

Recommendation: deny pooled trial credits. Options to offer:
A) 30-day paid pilot at discounted seat rate with usage-based top-up credits tied to a single billing entity; or
B) A monitored sandbox (limited tokens per team) subject to audit; require signed mutual action plan (MAP).

If Alex wants to keep the commercial motion open, propose A with a capped limited-time offer. If Concilio insists on free credits, escalate for account freeze and legal review.

Neha Kapoor
Fraud & Trust Analyst

Hi Sofia — thank you for the fast turnaround. We reviewed the request and found inconsistent account signals (multiple prior extensions, overlapping device fingerprints and shared billing artifacts) that prevent us from issuing a pooled free-credit grant at this time.

Wed like to keep working with you and propose two commercial next steps:
1) A 30-day paid pilot with a one-time 40% discount on seat pricing + a 100k token starter credit tied to a single billing entity; or
2) A monitored sandbox with three separate limited-usage seats (25k tokens each), subject to audit every 7 days and a signed MAP.

If you can provide signed confirmations from the named team owners and consolidate billing under a single purchasing contact, we can revisit a larger credit allocation.

Please let me know which option you prefer and I"ll get pricing and the MAP template over. If you need more time, we can set a short call.
